description:
GH #296. Page: /Users/j5n/Workspace/gh-296-297.html (Proposal B). PRODUCT_DRIVE_BUDGET is a flat 50,000 requests PER DRIVE (one drive_root_product_with call; a compile runs 1 to 47 drives, one per root session plus a Program drive). A tuple of 308 computed elements compiles (49,548 requests in its largest drive), 400 does not (82,622), 1,000 needs 505,922: about N^2/2 transport_shape products, nearly all distinct keys (1.01 requests per key, at most 3 pulls of one key).
Measured on develop ff4a75ada over all 791 fixtures (scratch s75e/, spike.patch): drives of 1,000+ requests stay at or below 1.51 requests per distinct key; small Program drives under 300 requests reach 3.67; no key is pulled more than 17 times.
The runaway side is unmeasured: no program in the repo produces a repeating drive; the budget tests cut a normal drive short with a tiny budget. So whether floor + ratio x distinct keys separates healthy from runaway is not shown.
Two things this is waiting on: (1) the design is the user's decision, since a ratio changes what runaway means, and the quadratic request count is itself a cost question (fz-1y9 is the related nested-pair cost); (2) fz-sc8.159 rewrites the pump in product_drive.rs, so a build bases on it. PullSession has no distinct-key counter today.
The tuple is incidental: 1,000 sequential calls whose results all stay live (a1 = f(1) ... a1000 = f(1000), then their sum; scratch s75e/seq1000.fz) need 1,009,384 requests on interp and print the right answer. The quadratic count belongs to a body split into one resume function per call, each capturing one more value (fz-d7w has the mechanism; fz-2un is the JIT panic the same program hits on run).
title: The product drive budget bounds repetition, not program size
